_note: Adapted from the Build prompt starters in Rocket's public docs (docs.rocket.new/learn/...). The structure and feature lists follow each starter; [placeholders] were filled with fictional products, and integrations (Supabase, Stripe, third-party APIs) are restated as locally mocked, because the sandbox has a fixed dependency set. Wording is paraphrased, not copied.

prompts.prompt: Build a landing page for Tidewell, a habit tracker for remote teams. Include a hero section with a headline, subheadline and primary call-to-action, three benefits each with an icon, a three-step 'How it works' section, two placeholder customer testimonials, a pricing section with Free and Pro tiers, and an email signup form that validates the address and shows a confirmation message. Modern, clean design.

Build a single-goal lead capture page for a free downloadable 'Remote Onboarding Checklist'. It needs a benefit-focused headline, a short list of four things the reader will learn, a form with name, work email and company fields (all required, with inline validation errors), a row of three placeholder company logos as social proof, and one strong call-to-action button. After a valid submission, replace the form with a thank-you message.

Build a one-page pitch site for Northbeam, a startup that predicts solar panel maintenance. Sections: the problem, the solution, four key metrics as placeholder numbers, a team section with four members (name, role, initials avatar), and a 'Get in touch' form with name, email and message. Premium, investor-ready style on a dark background with a single amber accent color.

Build a 'Ledgerly vs SheetBooks' comparison page for two fictional accounting tools. Include a feature comparison table with at least ten rows using check and cross marks, a section with Ledgerly's three key advantages, one testimonial from a customer who switched, a call-to-action, and an FAQ of four questions about switching that expand and collapse. Keep the tone objective.

Build a launch landing page for Quillbox, an AI meeting-notes app. Include a hero, a problem-to-solution section, a three-column benefits section, a three-step 'How it works' section, testimonials, three pricing tiers with a monthly/yearly billing toggle that updates the prices, a five-question FAQ accordion, and a footer with links.

Build a multi-screen onboarding flow for a project management app. Screens: a welcome screen; step 1 choose preferences (theme and notification frequency); step 2 connect an integration (pick one of Slack, GitHub or Google Drive — simulate the connection with a short loading state); step 3 invite team members by email (add and remove addresses, validate format); and a completion screen with a button to the main dashboard page. Show a progress indicator on every step, allow going back without losing answers, and add a simple dashboard page that greets the user with their chosen settings.

Build a prototype of an expense report submission feature. Flow: 1) list of the user's draft and submitted reports, 2) create a report and add line items (date, merchant, category, amount), 3) review screen with the total and a policy warning if any single item is over $500, 4) submit with a success state. Use realistic placeholder data, and include empty, loading and error states (simulate a failed submit with a retry button).

prompts.source_ref: learn/guides/prompt-library — Blog and content; learn/prompt-starters/for-marketers — Blog redesign
prompts.prompt: Build a blog with a featured-post hero, a card grid of at least eight posts, category filter chips, reading-time badges, author avatars and a newsletter signup. Each card links to its own post detail page with the full article, author, date and two related posts. Use local placeholder posts. Clean, Medium-like reading experience, responsive down to mobile.

Build a calendar app with a monthly grid view, previous/next month navigation, today highlighted, and a list of upcoming events beside the calendar. Users can click a day to create an event (title, date, start time, optional description), click an event to edit or delete it, and see a dot on days that have events. Keep events in client state, seeded with a few examples.

Build a product search page over a local catalogue of at least 30 items (name, category, price, rating). Include a search bar with debounced input, category filter, sort by price or rating, a result count, a 'no results' message with a clear-filters button, and keep the current query and filters in the URL so the page can be shared.

Build a full-stack CRUD app for managing invoices. Invoices have number, client, issue date, due date, line items, status (draft, sent, paid, overdue) and total. Include a data table that is sortable, filterable by status and paginated; create and edit forms with validation; a detail view; and a delete confirmation dialog. Persist data through Next.js route handlers backed by an in-memory store (no external database).

Build an operations dashboard that reads from a local API route returning mock order data. Show four summary metric cards, a time-series chart of orders per day for the last 30 days (draw it yourself with SVG — no chart library), and a data table with search and a status filter. Refresh the data automatically every 60 seconds and show when it was last updated, with loading and error states.

Build a SaaS MVP for Formwise, a form-builder product. Include sign-up, log-in and password-reset pages (mock the auth: accept any valid email and an 8+ character password, and keep the session in a cookie), a dashboard with key metrics, an account settings page, and a billing page where the user can switch between Free, Pro and Team plans (mock the payment step). Use a sidebar navigation layout, and redirect signed-out users away from app pages.

Build an online store for handmade ceramics with a product grid, category filters, search, and product detail pages (images as placeholders, description, price, stock). Add a shopping cart with quantity changes, removal and a running subtotal that persists across page reloads, and a checkout page with a shipping form and an order summary that ends in an order-confirmation screen. Use local product data.

Create a webhook endpoint at /api/webhooks/payments that accepts POST requests, verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature from the 'x-signature' header using a secret read from an environment variable, and returns 401 if verification fails. Route three event types (payment.succeeded, payment.failed, refund.created) to separate handlers, store each received event in memory, and add a page that lists the received events with type, time and payload, newest first.
